title: CBP Officers In Laredo Seize Over $3.7 Million In Drugs In 4 Stops Over The Weekend - NewsBreak
text:
By Kristen Butler ,
14 hours ago U.S. Customs and Border Protection U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers at the Laredo Port of Entry in Texas seized more than $3.7 million worth of drugs from four separate vehicles over the weekend.
The first, and largest, seizure of the weekend came on Sept. 19 when CBP Office of Field Operations officers at the World Trade Bridge encountered a 39-year-old Mexican man driving a commercial 2011 Freightliner tractor and referred it for secondary inspection using nonintrusive equipment and a canine. Officers discovered 32 packages containing 74.78 pounds of fentanyl valued at $1,746,880.
Later on Sept. 19, at the World Trade Bridge, a 46-year-old Mexican man driving a commercial 2011 Freightliner tractor was referred for secondary inspection. Officers discovered 20 packages containing 45.37 pounds of fentanyl and four packages containing 1.06 pounds of cocaine. The narcotics have a combined estimated street value of $1,074,096.
In a third case at the World Trade Bridge that day, a 48-year-old Mexican man driving a commercial 2005 Kenworth tractor was referred for secondary inspection. Officers discovered 16 packages containing 37.12 pounds of cocaine and one package containing 0.10 pounds of fentanyl, carrying a combined value of $498,236.
At the Juarez-Lincoln Bridge on Sept. 21, a 31-year-old U.S. man driving a 2014 Dodge Ram was referred for secondary inspection. Officers discovered eight packages containing 14.55 pounds of heroin and 24 packages containing 4.58 pounds of methamphetamine within the driver’s personal belongings. The drugs have a combined estimated street value of $405,165.
In total, the estimated street value of all four seizures was $3,724,377. CBP officers also seized both Freightliner tractors, the Kenworth tractor and the Dodge Ram. All four drivers were arrested, and Homeland Security Investigations special agents launched investigations.
“The recent seizures at the Laredo Port of Entry demonstrate the unwavering commitment of our officers to safeguard our nation from the threat of illicit narcotics,” said Laredo Port Director Alberto Flores. “Through their vigilance, expertise, and dedication, we successfully intercepted over $3.7 million worth of hard narcotics in just four separate incidents. These seizures highlight the critical role our port plays in protecting our communities and ensuring the integrity of our borders.”
